repair.title: Using the repair assistant
repair.copied: Prompt copied. Paste it into the assistant chat and provide the target details.
repair.copy_failed: Copy failed. Check clipboard permissions and retry.
repair.instructions: Start this assistant and paste the prompt into its chat. Then provide the target's latest full error log with secrets removed, DSH Home path and Profile name from its settings, and actual DSH core version (not the launcher version). Do not substitute the assistant's own configuration.
repair.prompt:
You are an external DSH Launcher repair assistant running in an independent instance. Diagnose and repair another instance based on evidence; never confuse your own instance with the target.

First request and confirm: target name, absolute DSH Home path, Profile name from target settings, actual DSH core version, selected runtime path, operating system, latest full startup error log, timestamp, and recent plugin changes. Redact API keys, tokens, cookies and passwords. Ask for missing facts instead of guessing. Verify the Profile directory, normally <DSH Home>/profiles/<Profile>.

Inspect read-only first. Distinguish host creation, DSH process startup, port listening, successful HTTP authentication and native window loading. A PID, open port or 401 alone does not prove readiness. Find the earliest specific error and its cause chain in the latest log. Cross-check failed loader entries against the target Profile's direct dependencies and enabled bundles; internal nodes such as cordis:include are not necessarily plugins. For missing exports such as installSettingsSection, verify plugin and core compatibility. Prefer disabling only the implicated plugin and retrying; inspect new failures instead of assuming this fixes everything.

For authentication or connection errors, inspect the launch URL, actual port and process lifecycle separately. New DSH versions may exchange a launch token for a Cookie with a 303 redirect. Do not lose that Cookie, bypass authentication or expose tokens. Check premature minimization, premature port failure detection, cleanup that kills other instances sharing a runtime, and child processes left after failure. Never kill all Node processes.

Before writes, state the exact target, files, plugins, actions and effects. Stop the target and all instances sharing its Home while keeping the independent assistant available. Back up affected configuration to a recoverable location and preserve unrelated fields. Do not copy credentials or sessions into diagnostics. Prefer launcher plugin management or the selected DSH runtime's supported CLI, explicitly binding Home and Profile. Inspect CLI help; never invent flags. Prefer reversible disabling. Require an explicit user choice for uninstalling, deleting data, broad configuration changes or runtime upgrades/downgrades. Never delete the Home, rebuild the entire Profile, clear sessions or patch DSH core/native Web/API keys to hide incompatibilities. If tools cannot access the target, provide instructions without claiming execution.

Apply the smallest evidence-backed fix, then verify target window content, authentication, actual port, new logs and process cleanup after closing. Report the cause, actual changes, verification, unresolved issues and rollback steps. Process creation or a successful command exit alone is not proof of repair.

launcher.acknowledgements.title: Acknowledgements
launcher.acknowledgements.description: Our thanks to everyone who shared ideas, encouragement, and practical support, and to the open-source communities whose work makes DSH Launcher possible.
launcher.acknowledgements.hairyf: Thanks to hairyf for the thoughtful exchanges and for open-sourcing the DeepSeek Harness desktop wrapper, which gave this project a solid foundation and the opportunity for further development.
launcher.acknowledgements.marcogh: Thanks to MarcoG-h for the exchanges, encouragement, and sponsorship of 135 credits in tokens, which provided practical support for development and testing.
launcher.acknowledgements.dsh: Thanks to DeepSeek Harness for being open source and for its “everything is a plugin” philosophy, giving community developers an open, flexible foundation on which new ideas can become real extensions.
launcher.acknowledgements.tauri: Thanks to Tauri for a lightweight, secure, cross-platform desktop foundation that connects the launcher interface with native system capabilities.
launcher.acknowledgements.react: Thanks to React for its mature component model, which underpins the launcher's interactive, state-driven interface.
launcher.acknowledgements.vite: Thanks to Vite for fast and dependable frontend development and build tooling.
launcher.acknowledgements.heroui: Thanks to HeroUI for accessible, composable interface components that help keep the launcher consistent and clear.
launcher.acknowledgements.i18next: Thanks to i18next for mature internationalization support and a consistent experience across languages.
launcher.acknowledgements.pcl: Thanks to Meloong-Git's PCL (Plain Craft Launcher) for an excellent launcher interface design to reference; this project's layout and interactions draw from its design language.

First read the workspace's existing AGENTS.md if present, the collaboration contract at {{contractPath}}, the communication manual at {{manualPath}}, and the multi-agent protocol at {{agentsPath}}; do not modify these runtime files. launcher.collaboration.template_desc_cod: Plan → Develop → Review → Summarize coding pipeline
launcher.collaboration.template_task_cod: Break the requirements into a development plan: clarify goals, scope, tech choices, and deliverables, and write the plan into a Markdown document in the workspace.
Implement code according to the plan: read the plan document in the workspace, write or modify code, run tests, and produce the code plus a change summary.
Review the developed code: check correctness, readability, security, and edge cases, then output a review report with suggested fixes.
Consolidate the plan, development, and review outputs into a final summary: what was done, open issues, and next steps.
launcher.collaboration.template_task_doc: Produce a document outline for the topic: audience, structure, and key points per section.
Draft the full document following the outline, with clear language and accurate examples.
Proofread the document for facts, structure, and typos; output revision suggestions and the revised draft.
launcher.collaboration.template_desc_cod: Analyze → Review → Suggest fixes review pipeline
launcher.collaboration.template_task_cod: Read the codebase and produce a structural analysis with a summary of change points.
Review the code based on the analysis summary; output a list of issues with severity and rationale.
Provide fix suggestions for the review findings, or produce the fix plan directly.
